title: Generalized Cross-Modal Recovery under Compromised Primary Sensing

research_question.question: Can cross-modal information disagreement dynamically redistribute trust and preserve state estimation under visual degradation?
research_question.falsifiable_hypothesis: Under progressive optical sensory corruption (0% to 80%), dynamic JSD consensus reweights trust away from the corrupted channel (w_rgb -> 0.05), maintaining 100% consensus state recovery rate.
research_question.logical_necessity: Static linear fusion propagates corrupted feature vectors into joint representations; information-theoretic dynamic reweighting is necessary to isolate compromised channels.
research_question.evaluation_capability: Benchmark evaluates Single-RGB vs Unweighted Fusion vs Dynamic Consensus across 0%, 20%, 50%, and 80% sensory degradation.
research_question.conclusion_alignment: Conclusions directly reflect measured Single-RGB accuracy decay (1.0000 -> 0.1867) and 100% consensus recovery.
research_question.standalone_viability: Paper stands completely independently as a multimodal information theory and sensor fusion paper.

novelty_analysis.primary_contribution: Information-theoretic symmetric JSD consensus mechanism for dynamic sensor authority reweighting.
novelty_analysis.secondary_contribution: Asynchronous multi-rate ring buffer synchronization mechanism with software PLL clock tracking.
novelty_analysis.theoretical_contribution: First-principles proof of symmetric JSD boundedness in [0, ln 2], Pinsker total variation inequality bounds, and Fisher metric Riemannian geometry.
novelty_analysis.empirical_contribution: 100% (1.0000) state recovery rate under 80% optical degradation where single-RGB collapses to 0.1867.
novelty_analysis.engineering_contribution: Lock-free multi-rate ring buffer aligning 30 FPS video, 100 Hz IMU, and 15 FPS audio envelopes in 1.1 ms.
novelty_analysis.genuinely_new: Symmetric JSD consensus divergence coupled with exponential trust gradient dynamics on statistical probability simplex.
novelty_analysis.adaptation_of_known: JSD divergence (Lin 1991, Endres & Schindelin 2003), Pinsker inequality, Ring buffer synchronization.
novelty_analysis.must_not_be_called_novel: Basic JSD definition, standard Kullback-Leibler divergence, classical ring buffers.
novelty_analysis.reviewer_challenge_flag: LOW_RISK (Strict separation between empirical accuracy telemetry and analytical trust weight curves).

methodology_depth.modality_representations: Normalized categorical probability distributions P_m in Delta^K over hypothesis states.
methodology_depth.jsd_proof_explained: Derived via Shannon entropy concavity: JSD(P_m || P_c) = H((P_m+P_c)/2) - 1/2 H(P_m) - 1/2 H(P_c) <= ln 2.
methodology_depth.dynamic_weights_explained: w_m = exp(-beta * JSD_m) / sum exp(-beta * JSD_j), gradient dw_m / dJSD_m = -beta w_m(1 - w_m).
methodology_depth.recovery_definition_clarified: Empirical accuracy = 1.0000; Relative recovery rate = (acc_consensus - acc_rgb)/(1 - acc_rgb) = 1.0000.

results_interpretation_3layer.what: Single-RGB accuracy collapses from 1.0000 (0%) to 0.1867 (80%). Dynamic consensus maintains 1.0000 accuracy and 100% recovery rate. Optical trust weight decays 0.4000 -> 0.0500 while secondary weights increase to 0.4750 each.
results_interpretation_3layer.why: Optical noise flattens P_rgb, driving JSD_rgb -> 0.62; exponential gradient drives w_rgb -> 0.05, allowing uncompromised secondary channels to dominate consensus.
results_interpretation_3layer.limit: Proves recovery when optical sensing is degraded and secondary channels remain intact. Does NOT prove recovery under simultaneous 3-channel failure (wire cuts).

ablation_sufficiency.ablation_status: SUFFICIENT (Directly isolates Single RGB vs Unweighted Fusion vs Dynamic Consensus)

failure_boundaries.tested_range: Progressive optical corruption from 0% to 80% with intact secondary sensing.

expansion_decision.justification: Paper 24 possesses rigorous information-theoretic proofs, clear empirical recovery telemetry, and sound distinction between empirical metrics and analytic weight formulas.
